speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. You mentioned increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with episodes of pain during urination. To understand this better, have you noticed any redness or warmth over the affected knee joint?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's Syndrome)

The clinical picture of inflammatory arthritis (knee and ankle), urethritis (pain with urination), and high-risk sexual behavior in a 17-year-old male is highly suggestive of Reactive Arthritis. I will request a Urinalysis, HLA-B27 test, and joint fluid analysis to confirm the diagnosis and rule out gout or infection.
